episode_title: Building the Savannah Bananas (with Jesse Cole, Founder and Owner)
question: How did Jesse Cole transform the Gastonia Grizzlies from losing $150,000 annually to becoming fourth in the country in attendance?
transcript_excerpt: Cole realized at age 23 as GM of a team with only 200 fans and $268 in the bank that they could never compete on talent alone, so he began studying P.T. Barnum, Walt Disney, and entertainment figures to make the games more about entertainment than baseball. He experimented for 10 years with grandma beauty pageants, flatulence fun nights, salute to underwear nights, and having players dance during games. This eventually climbed them to fourth in the country in attendance, made the team profitable, and sold out games, though they only received one media story during that decade.

episode_title: Building the Savannah Bananas (with Jesse Cole, Founder and Owner)
question: What happened when the Savannah Bananas launched and why did Jesse Cole sell his house within three months?
transcript_excerpt: The Bananas launched on October 4-5, 2015, into complete rejection from the community that had just lost their official minor league team to Columbia, South Carolina. Within three months, Cole had sold only a handful of tickets despite hosting a free launch event. By January 15, 2016, they had overdrafted their account and were completely out of money, forcing Cole and his wife Emily to sell their house in Gastonia, empty their savings account, and move into a garage-turned-studio in Savannah where they slept on a twin airbed and grocery shopped with just $30 per week.

episode_title: Building the Savannah Bananas (with Jesse Cole, Founder and Owner)
question: Why did the Savannah Bananas choose the name 'Bananas' after running a naming contest?
transcript_excerpt: After receiving a thousand generic naming suggestions including spirits, ports, and anchors, a 62-year-old nurse named Lynn Moses suggested 'Bananas.' Cole and his team had already been thinking about the name and had developed complementary concepts including a senior citizen dance team called the Banana Nanas, a male cheerleading team called the Mananas, and a mascot named Split. Though the community initially criticized the name heavily and even booed Cole and his staff at Savannah's St. Patrick's Day parade, Cole believed the name and logo were bold enough to work and could not be criticized once properly executed.

episode_title: Building the Savannah Bananas (with Jesse Cole, Founder and Owner)
question: What is the Savannah Bananas' current business scale and ticket pricing model?
transcript_excerpt: The Savannah Bananas sold one million tickets last year and two million tickets the current year, with an additional 3.2 million person waiting list. Tickets are priced at approximately $35 per game with unlimited food and drinks included and no hidden fees. The team has over 15 million followers on social media, including more TikTok followers than every MLB team combined.

episode_title: Building the Savannah Bananas (with Jesse Cole, Founder and Owner)
question: What are the main rules of Banana Ball that differentiate it from traditional baseball?
transcript_excerpt: Banana Ball features a man on stilts performing during games, choreographed dances by players, and approximately 15 unique rules including: if a fan catches your foul ball you are out, if you bunt you are ejected, and various other modifications to traditional baseball gameplay designed to create entertainment-focused play.

episode_title: Building the Savannah Bananas (with Jesse Cole, Founder and Owner)
question: What financial deal did the Savannah Bananas negotiate to operate at the historic Grayson Stadium?
transcript_excerpt: The Savannah Bananas convinced the city of Savannah to lease them the historic Grayson Stadium (a 1926 ballpark where Babe Ruth, Hank Aaron, and Jackie Robinson played) for $20,000 per year after the previous minor league team demanded a $38 million new stadium and left for Columbia, South Carolina. Cole used the precedent from his Gastonia team to convince the city to support a college summer team at this legacy venue.
